_comment: Startup model recommendations, chosen by how much memory a machine has.
Edit this file to change what Brazier suggests. A copy placed at
<data>/model-recipes/recommendations.json replaces this one wholesale, so
recommendations can be updated without rebuilding the application.
Every entry carries an `id`. Changing the id is what tells Brazier the
recommendation for that category has changed, which is what triggers the
offer to swap for anyone who installed the previous one through the welcome
flow. Correcting a label or a note without changing the model should leave
the id alone.
`quant: by_memory` resolves at display time against the repository's real
file sizes: the best of Q8_0, Q6_K, Q5_K_M, Q4_K_M, Q3_K_M, Q2_K that fits
in 60% of usable memory, preferring Unsloth's UD-*_XL build of that rung.
The remaining 40% is left for the KV cache, the OS, and everything else.
A tier with no `agent` entry uses its `text` one. A category set to null is
offered nothing at that tier. `agent_options` adds optional agent cards after
the default agent; each has its own explanation and exact quant selection.
`computer_use` recommends a screenshot-driven agent model (Fara1.5). Its
vision projector is discovered automatically at resolve time, so the entry
only names the repository. Fara1.5 natively supports up to 262k context;
keep at least ~15k for multi-step trajectories.

text.label: Bonsai 27B (1-bit)

fallback.label: Qwen 3.5 9B
fallback.summary: A capable 9B Qwen model that runs with mainline llama.cpp.

text.summary: A Qwen3.6-27B derivative reduced to 1.125 bits per weight — a ~3.9GB footprint and ~90% of FP16 intelligence. Held back with room for the OS and a useful context window. The Q8 vision projector comes along so image input is also available.

image.label: Stable Diffusion 1.5
image.summary: Small, fast, and endlessly finetuned. A 512px image in seconds on almost any machine.

computer_use.label: Fara1.5 4B
computer_use.summary: Microsoft's smallest computer-use model. It reads screenshots and drives the browser or desktop with click and type actions. Fits this tier with room for a useful context window.

text.label: Bonsai 27B (ternary)

fallback.label: Qwen 3.5 9B
fallback.summary: A capable 9B Qwen model that runs with mainline llama.cpp.

text.summary: The same Qwen3.6-27B derivative at 2-bit ternary weights — ~5.9GB and ~95% of FP16 intelligence. Uses the Q2_g64 build, which runs on current upstream llama.cpp. Fuller quality than the 1-bit build, well within this machine's budget. The Q8 vision projector comes along so image input is also available.

image.label: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium
image.summary: A 2.6B MMDiT model with strong prompt adherence on harder text. A clearer step up from SDXL than FLUX is at this tier.

video.label: Wan 2.1 T2V 1.3B
video.summary: A practical text-to-video model for 16 GB machines. The larger Wan 2.2 image-to-video model needs more memory.

computer_use.label: Fara1.5 9B
computer_use.summary: Microsoft's mid-size computer-use model. Reads screenshots and drives the browser or desktop with click and type actions. The Q5 build leaves room for the vision projector and a long trajectory.

text.summary: A 26B mixture-of-experts model with 4B active, so it answers at roughly the speed of a much smaller model while knowing much more.

voice.summary: Realtime voice needs two models rather than one: PersonaPlex speaks and listens, and a separate recogniser turns what you say into text. Both are small enough that the same pair suits every machine.

models.label: PersonaPlex
models.summary: Full-duplex speech in and speech out. Requires accepting the model license on Hugging Face.

models.label: Whisper base
models.summary: Transcribes your spoken turns, which PersonaPlex does not report on its own.
